claims.text: Incorporating oxygen-induced lattice defects and their scattering effects will improve electrical- and thermal-conductivity predictions for bulk HfNbTaTiZr relative to defect-free analytical models.
The targeted bulk HfNbTaTiZr contains approximately 1 wt.% oxygen.
A multiscale framework will combine physical models of defect-induced electron and phonon scattering with machine-learning calibration.
The proposed model is intended to cover the 0–200 K and 300–1200 K temperature regimes.
Oxygen produces point defects and associated lattice disorder in HfNbTaTiZr.
Oxygen-induced point defects and lattice disorder act as additional electron-scattering centers.
Oxygen-induced point defects and lattice disorder act as additional phonon-scattering centers.
Explicitly modeling oxygen-related defect scattering will move conductivity predictions away from perfect-crystal predictions and reduce predictive error.
The defect-inclusive model will produce conductivity predictions significantly closer to experiment than traditional analytical approaches.
Conventional analytical conductivity models for the comparison assume perfect, defect-free crystals.
Conventional analytical models show substantial discrepancies from experiment because they neglect defect and impurity scattering.
The approach is applicable to bulk HfNbTaTiZr containing up to approximately 1 wt.% oxygen within 0–200 K and 300–1200 K.
The approach's accuracy outside the stated oxygen content and temperature windows is untested.
Limited calibration data and temperature-dependent scattering make the magnitude of improvement uncertain.
